name: Matera
tagline: Ancient cave city carved into a ravine
summary: Matera is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on Earth, its Sassi cave dwellings stacked up the side of a ravine. Explore rock-cut churches with Byzantine frescoes, step inside a furnished cave house, sleep in a cave hotel, and cross the gorge to the Murgia park for the view back at the lit-up town.
seasonNote: Spring and early autumn are ideal; summer is hot, and the 2 July Bruna festival fills the town.
arrival: Bari airport is about 1 hour by shuttle bus or car; Ferrovie Appulo Lucane trains run from Bari.
gettingAround: Walk the Sassi (lots of steps); taxis or a car for the Murgia park.
cashTip: Cards are widely accepted, but carry cash for bars, markets and small trattorie. A coperto (cover charge) is normal; tipping is optional.
foodTip: Pane di Matera bread, crapiata bean soup, peperoni cruschi (crispy dried peppers) and orecchiette.
baseArea: Sasso Barisano or Sasso Caveoso, in a cave hotel

connections.note: About an hour to Alberobello and the Bari area.
